Guidance & outlook: As per the Second Advance Estimates released by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the revised 2022-23 base year, India's real GDP is estimated to have grown by 7.6% in FY 2025 -26, an improvement over the revised 6.5% (formerly reported as 6.5%, now restated under the new base) recorded in FY 2024 -25.
EBITDA EBITDA for FY 2025 -26 stood at ₹2,392.44 Lakhs, compared to ₹2,321.53 Lakhs in FY 2024 -25, representing a modest improvement despite the decline in revenue.

Finance Costs Finance costs for FY 2025 -26 were ₹1,195.73 Lakhs, broadly stable compared to ₹1,196.69 Lakhs in FY 2024-25 and significantly lower than ₹1,421.55 Lakhs in FY 2023 -24, despite a meaningfully larger capital employed base during the year.
Growth & demand: Global real GDP growth moderated to approximately 3.2% in 2025 and is estimated at 3.1% for 2026 - a downward revision from earlier projections, primarily reflecting the economic impact of the conflict in the Middle East and its effect on oil markets and global supply chains.

Advanced Economies grew at approximately 1.5% in 2025, with growth expected to improve marginally to 1.8% in 2026 supported by fiscal stimulus and lower policy rates in several major economies, including the United States.

The domestic ceramic tile market is estimated at approximately USD 10.45 billion in 2025, with industry research project ing growth to around USD 11.30 billion in 2026 and further expansion at a compound annual growth rate of approximately 8 -10% over the medium term.
Margins & costs: Headline CPI inflation fell to an eight -year low during the year before edging up modestly, and the RBI revised its full -year inflation forecast downward to around 2.1 -2.6% - significantly below its medium -term target.
This reflects an improved EBITDA margin for the year, supported by disciplined control over employee costs and operating overheads even as material costs rose.

Profit Before Tax (PBT) and Profit After Tax (PAT) PBT for FY 2025-26 increased significantly to ₹301.16 Lakhs, compared to ₹173.07 Lakhs in FY 2024-25, notwithstanding the decline in revenue, aided by improved EBITDA performance and stable finance costs.
Capex & expansion: On the fiscal front, the Union Budget 2025 -26 maintained its focus on capital expenditure, with effective capex reaching around 4% of GDP, while revenue expenditure continued to moderate as a share of GDP, creating fiscal space for sustained infrastruc ture investment.

Both manufacturing units at Padra and Talod operated through the year, with the combined facility a chieving an installed capacity of approximately 1.32 crore square metres and actual production of approximately 1.05 crore square metres, representing an overall capacity utilization of 80%.

Plant-wise Installed Capacity vs Actual Production (FY 2025-26) The Padra plant operated at a healthy utilization level of 84%, while the Talod plant operated at 77% utilization, reflecting strong overall asset productivity across the Company's manufacturing footprint.

Capital Employed, Net Worth and Borrowings Capital employed increased to ₹36,937.45 Lakhs for FY 2025 -26, compared to ₹30,540.42 Lakhs in FY 2024-25, reflecting incremental investment in the Company's asset base and working capital.
Risks & challenges: Risk Management Committee The Company is not required to constitute the Risk Management Committee , as the provision of Regulation 21 of the Listing Regulations is not applicable to the Company.
